title: "AI makes games in 5 minutes now." Cool. Here's what months of making one with AI actually looked like
author: KurnazBen
selftext:
Typed "make me a co-op game" and went to get coffee. Came back months later, still fixing things.



The game is Dungeon Shop Simulator: 1-4 player online co-op, dungeons at night, your own shop by day.



What the AI tools actually did:

\- Claude Code: pair programmer for most of the code, plus notes it keeps so it remembers the project between sessions

\- Meshy: base 3D models from my own concept images, then cleanup, retopo, rigging and textures in Blender

\- ElevenLabs: intro narration

\- Translations into 20 languages, reviewed by me



What they absolutely did not do:

\- Tell me what's fun. That took playtests with friends that kept turning into 6-hour sessions.

\- Fix co-op desync on their own. Every "it works" had to be tested by real people on real connections.

\- Keep a consistent art style. That needed a locked style prompt and a lot of rejected models.

\- Balance an economy where players set their own prices.



Steam page went live today, release planned for March 2027. Ask me anything about the pipeline.

replies.author: QTpopOfficial
replies.body:
Tutorials are an art and if you don't understand user friction and customer retention making a tutorial is a lot harder.

You need to give people options to opt out, as well as keep the "Full tutorial" as short as possible while still delivering dopamine during it. Every single time you take control away to read a text box, you've added friction.

Thats my TL:DR version without major context on how to make tutorials. lol

replies.author: QTpopOfficial
replies.body:
Your friends will sugar coat things. Do you think my "Friends" are going to be honest about things outside of actual industry buddies who won't hold back because they know better?

If someone told you the tutorial sucks. Look into it. Someone tells you that your text boxes are too much. Look into it. Someone else gives you tips? Look into it.

It may not seem it, but theres actual real advice there.
